hook_text: A stone cross on a windy point in the Eastern Cape, placed there in 1488. Why would sailors carry a cross across the ocean?
clip_script: Kwaaihoek, near Kenton-on-Sea. A copy of a stone cross, called a padrão, stands on the point. Dias placed the original here in 1488. Portuguese explorers carried stone crosses to claim land for their king and to show their Christian faith. They hoped to spread Christianity and to find Christian allies, like the legendary Prester John. And they wanted to find the East: Portugal sailed around Africa, while Spain sent Columbus west. God, gold and glory.
visual_style: Whiteboard dunes and a rocky point with a stone cross, then a world map with one route around Africa and another across the Atlantic.
mood: Windswept and thoughtful, like standing where history happened.
pacing: Slow walk to the cross, a pause, then two routes drawn on the map.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and trace the Portuguese and Spanish routes on a world map.
